findings.title: Resource lookup resolves inherited Object.prototype keys (GET /constructor returns 200 with empty body, PUT /toString creates a resource)
findings.property: unknown resource names give 404, never a 200 or a mutation
findings.expected: 404 Not Found for both; db.data gains no 'toString' key
findings.actual: GET /constructor returns 200 with an empty body (the Object function is serialized); PUT /toString returns 200 and writes an own 'toString' key into db.data
findings.evidence: Service.#get does this.#db.data[name] without an own-property check, although Service.has() exists and uses hasOwnProperty; the final handler returns 404 whenever the lookup yields undefined, which shows unknown names are meant to be 404.

review.title: Resource lookup resolves inherited Object.prototype keys (GET /constructor returns 200, PUT /toString creates a resource)
review.reason: `Service.#get` (src/service.ts:88) returns `this.#db.data[name]` with no own-property check, so a name like `constructor` or `toString` yields an inherited function instead of `undefined`. The 404 handler in app.ts only triggers when the lookup is `undefined`, so GET returns 200 with a serialized function. `#updateOrPatch` then runs `this.#db.data[name] = body`, which writes an own key into the db for a resource that never existed. The repro is valid, and `Service.has()` already shows the intended own-property semantics. The fix is a one-line `hasOwnProperty` guard in `#get`, which a maintainer would likely accept, though the impact is small for a local mock server.
